descVi: Chính sách công, luật pháp, quyền công dân và quản trị quốc gia.

words.definitionEn: To make certain that something happens or is true
words.exampleDailyEn: Please ensure that all windows are closed before leaving.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should ensure that affordable public transport is available to residents in both urban and rural areas.

words.definitionEn: to give official permission for an activity
words.exampleDailyEn: You need a license to drive on public roads.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Authorities should license childcare providers carefully to ensure that facilities meet appropriate safety and quality standards.

words.definitionEn: To officially forbid an action through rules or laws.
words.exampleDailyEn: The pool rules prohibit running on the wet floor.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should prohibit the dumping of untreated industrial waste into rivers to protect public health.

words.definitionEn: control an activity through rules or laws
words.exampleDailyEn: This small device helps regulate the temperature indoors.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should regulate industrial emissions to protect public health without placing unnecessary burdens on small businesses.

words.definitionEn: to limit what someone can do or how much is allowed
words.exampleDailyEn: These tight shoes restrict my movement when I dance.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities may restrict private vehicle access to city centres in order to reduce air pollution.

words.definitionEn: a rule or condition that limits what is allowed
words.exampleDailyEn: There is a parking restriction outside our building today.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Restrictions on private car use may encourage commuters to choose more sustainable forms of transport.

words.definitionEn: an act that breaks a law, rule, or agreement
words.exampleDailyEn: Parking across this entrance is a clear violation.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Collecting personal information without consent may constitute a violation of privacy, even when the data remains confidential.

words.definitionEn: the power or right to make decisions and enforce rules
words.exampleDailyEn: Only the manager has authority to approve this refund.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should consult residents before introducing policies that significantly affect access to public services.

words.definitionEn: An official group appointed to investigate or manage something
words.exampleDailyEn: The gallery commissioned a local artist to paint our harbour.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An independent commission should investigate housing conditions before the government introduces new safety regulations for rental properties.

words.definitionEn: money given by an organisation for a particular purpose
words.exampleDailyEn: A small grant helped us repair the village playground.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should provide research grants to universities developing affordable technologies for reducing household energy consumption.

words.definitionEn: to put a plan or decision into action
words.exampleDailyEn: Our team will implement the new schedule next week.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should implement policies that make public transport more affordable for people on low incomes.

words.definitionEn: Officially introduce a rule, tax, punishment, or restriction
words.exampleDailyEn: The library imposed a small fine for my overdue books.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments may impose higher taxes on sugary drinks to encourage healthier choices and reduce public healthcare costs.

words.definitionEn: relating to armed forces or their activities
words.exampleDailyEn: We watched military helicopters carry supplies to the island.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments must balance military spending with investment in essential public services such as healthcare and education.

words.definitionEn: a government department responsible for a particular area
words.exampleDailyEn: My aunt works at the ministry near the station.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The education ministry should consult teachers before introducing major changes to the national school curriculum.

words.definitionEn: An official rule controlling how something must be done.
words.exampleDailyEn: Safety regulations require everyone here to wear a helmet.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Stricter regulation of industrial waste could reduce water pollution and improve public health in nearby communities.

words.definitionEn: A partnership between groups or countries pursuing shared goals.
words.exampleDailyEn: The two clubs formed an alliance to save the pool.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An international alliance can help countries coordinate their responses to environmental threats that cross national borders.

words.definitionEn: a formal agreement between countries
words.exampleDailyEn: We heard about the new treaty on the radio.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An international treaty can establish shared environmental standards, but its success depends on effective enforcement.

words.definitionEn: A country whose head of state is not a monarch.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our teacher explained how the country became a republic.
words.exampleIeltsEn: In a republic, constitutional rules usually define the powers of the head of state and other public institutions.

words.definitionEn: to officially end a law, system, or established practice
words.exampleDailyEn: Our library has abolished fines for returning books late.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Some economists argue that governments should abolish subsidies that encourage excessive consumption of fossil fuels.

words.definitionEn: A person or country that supports another.
words.exampleDailyEn: My neighbour became an ally in saving the park.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local charities can be valuable allies for governments seeking to reduce poverty and improve social inclusion.

words.definitionEn: A senior official representing their country in another country.
words.exampleDailyEn: The ambassador welcomed visitors to the embassy garden.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An ambassador can strengthen international cooperation by encouraging educational exchanges and maintaining dialogue during periods of tension.

words.definitionEn: Weapons and military equipment.
words.exampleDailyEn: The museum displays old arms behind thick glass.
words.exampleIeltsEn: International agreements can restrict the trade in arms and encourage governments to resolve disputes peacefully.

words.definitionEn: to fight against something harmful
words.exampleDailyEn: We opened the windows to combat the afternoon heat.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments can combat air pollution by improving public transport and enforcing stricter limits on industrial emissions.

words.definitionEn: An official or public statement expressing a decision, belief, or intention.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her declaration that she would quit surprised the whole family.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The government's declaration of a climate emergency should be followed by clear policies and measurable environmental targets.

words.definitionEn: to announce something publicly or officially
words.exampleDailyEn: The judges declared her the winner of the competition.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities may declare a public holiday to encourage participation in an important community celebration.

words.definitionEn: Extreme or severe, causing a major change
words.exampleDailyEn: We took drastic action and sold our second car.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Drastic cuts to public transport funding could leave many low-income households without affordable access to essential services.

words.definitionEn: to choose someone for a position by voting
words.exampleDailyEn: Our club elected a new captain last night.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Citizens should elect representatives who are willing to address long-term environmental challenges rather than seek immediate popularity.

words.definitionEn: To order someone not to do something or disallow it
words.exampleDailyEn: Our building rules forbid leaving bicycles in the hallway.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should forbid companies from releasing untreated waste into rivers to protect public health and aquatic ecosystems.

words.definitionEn: To put someone in prison or keep them confined.
words.exampleDailyEn: The judge imprisoned the thief for stealing valuable paintings.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should consider whether imprisoning people for minor offences is more effective than providing supervised community service.

words.definitionEn: Make a determined effort to deal with a difficult problem.
words.exampleDailyEn: Let's tackle the messy kitchen before our guests arrive.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments need to tackle housing shortages by supporting affordable construction and improving access to public transport.

words.definitionEn: To assign resources to particular people, activities, or purposes.
words.exampleDailyEn: We allocated one cupboard to all our baking equipment.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should allocate more funding to public transport in areas with limited access to essential services.

words.definitionEn: To change a document, rule, or plan to improve it.
words.exampleDailyEn: Please amend the booking to include one extra guest.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Parliament may amend existing legislation to ensure that remote workers receive the same protections as office employees.

words.definitionEn: A change made to a law, document, or proposal.
words.exampleDailyEn: We agreed on one small amendment to the contract.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The proposed amendment would require employers to provide safer working conditions for temporary staff.

words.definitionEn: to make something no longer legally or officially acceptable
words.exampleDailyEn: Opening the device yourself may invalidate its warranty.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A sample that excludes older adults may invalidate conclusions about the health needs of the wider population.

words.definitionEn: To act against a law, rule, or agreement.
words.exampleDailyEn: Leaving your car here violates the building's parking rules.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Collecting personal data without informed consent may violate citizens' privacy and undermine public trust in digital services.

words.definitionEn: an official responsible for a public service or commission
words.exampleDailyEn: The commissioner visited our neighbourhood to discuss road safety.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An independent commissioner should investigate public complaints and ensure that government agencies treat citizens fairly.

words.definitionEn: a person living in an area represented by an elected official
words.exampleDailyEn: A constituent asked her local representative about the closed library.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Elected representatives should consult their constituents before supporting policies that significantly affect local housing and public transport.

words.definitionEn: Make sure that people obey a law or rule.
words.exampleDailyEn: The pool staff enforce strict rules about running indoors.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments must enforce environmental regulations consistently if they want industries to reduce pollution and protect public health.

words.definitionEn: Greater importance that gives someone or something priority over others.
words.exampleDailyEn: At home, homework takes precedence over video games.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public safety should take precedence over commercial interests when governments develop regulations for new transport technologies.

words.definitionEn: a government or system of government, especially an authoritarian one
words.exampleDailyEn: The new regime promised to reopen the public library.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An authoritarian regime may restrict public debate, making it harder for citizens to influence government decisions.

words.definitionEn: Limiting what people can do or what is allowed.
words.exampleDailyEn: The club's restrictive rules prevent us from bringing guests.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Overly restrictive planning regulations can discourage investment and delay the construction of affordable housing.

words.definitionEn: The freedom or right to make decisions independently.
words.exampleDailyEn: My new manager gives me more autonomy at work.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Giving schools greater autonomy may help teachers adapt their lessons to the specific needs of local communities.

words.definitionEn: Likely to experience something, especially something unpleasant.
words.exampleDailyEn: These old pipes are liable to burst in winter.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Employers may be held liable for injuries caused by unsafe conditions in the workplace.

words.definitionEn: Having no legal force or effect.
words.exampleDailyEn: The court declared their rental agreement null and void.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A contract may be declared null if one party was forced to accept its terms.

words.definitionEn: A formal agreement between countries, groups, or organisations.
words.exampleDailyEn: The two clubs reached an accord over sharing equipment.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An international accord on emissions could encourage countries to adopt cleaner technologies and protect vulnerable ecosystems.

words.definitionEn: Loyalty and support given to a country, group, or leader.
words.exampleDailyEn: Despite moving abroad, he kept his allegiance to his hometown club.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Political allegiance can influence how voters interpret economic policies and assess the performance of elected officials.

words.definitionEn: Protection a country gives people escaping danger in another country.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her family sought asylum after fleeing their home country.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should assess asylum applications fairly while ensuring that vulnerable applicants have access to legal advice.

words.definitionEn: To give official permission for someone to do something.
words.exampleDailyEn: Only the manager can authorize a refund this large.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities may authorize new housing developments only after assessing their likely effects on traffic and public services.

words.definitionEn: A group of countries or people acting together for shared aims.
words.exampleDailyEn: The councillors formed a bloc to protect local parks.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A regional trading bloc can strengthen members' bargaining power while reducing barriers to trade between participating countries.

words.definitionEn: an office or organisation providing information or managing particular activities
words.exampleDailyEn: The tourist bureau gave us a free city map.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A national statistics bureau collects reliable data that governments use to plan public services.

words.definitionEn: To approach people and ask for their votes or support.
words.exampleDailyEn: Volunteers canvassed the neighbourhood before the local election.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should canvass residents' views before introducing major changes to public transport routes and schedules.

words.definitionEn: the act of following a rule, law, or request
words.exampleDailyEn: The inspector checked our kitchen for compliance with hygiene rules.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular inspections can improve compliance with environmental regulations and reduce pollution from industrial facilities.

words.definitionEn: to limit or control something unwanted
words.exampleDailyEn: I try to curb my spending by cooking at home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Cities can curb air pollution by improving public transport and encouraging residents to cycle.

words.definitionEn: An official order issued by a ruler, government, or court.
words.exampleDailyEn: The new decree means our street stays closed tonight.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The government issued a decree requiring factories to treat wastewater before releasing it into rivers.

words.definitionEn: To officially choose someone or something for a particular purpose.
words.exampleDailyEn: We designated one cupboard for all our cleaning supplies.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should designate more urban land as protected green space to improve residents' quality of life.

words.definitionEn: The act of officially choosing someone or something for a purpose.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her designation as team leader surprised nobody at work.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The designation of coastal wetlands as protected areas can help preserve biodiversity and limit inappropriate development.

words.definitionEn: in a clear and direct way that leaves no doubt
words.exampleDailyEn: I expressly asked for a room away from the lift.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public funds allocated expressly for environmental protection should not be diverted to projects that increase industrial pollution.

words.definitionEn: A subgroup whose views conflict with others in a larger group.
words.exampleDailyEn: One faction of our club wants a new leader.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A powerful faction within the ruling party opposed the proposed reforms to the national education system.

words.definitionEn: Extremely important and needing to be done.
words.exampleDailyEn: It is imperative to keep this medicine refrigerated.
words.exampleIeltsEn: As urban populations grow, it is imperative that governments invest in reliable and affordable public transport.

words.definitionEn: An action that breaks a law or violates someone's rights.
words.exampleDailyEn: Copying that photograph without permission could be copyright infringement.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should protect creative workers by imposing appropriate penalties for the infringement of intellectual property rights.

words.definitionEn: allowed or recognised by law
words.exampleDailyEn: The lost bicycle was returned to its lawful owner.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should ensure that personal information is collected only for lawful purposes and protected against misuse.

words.definitionEn: Not strict or careful enough about rules or responsibilities.
words.exampleDailyEn: The club is lax about checking membership cards.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Lax enforcement of environmental regulations allows some factories to discharge untreated waste into nearby rivers.

words.definitionEn: less strict or severe when enforcing rules or giving punishment
words.exampleDailyEn: Our teacher was lenient when I submitted homework late.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Some argue that lenient penalties for illegal dumping fail to discourage companies from damaging the environment.

words.definitionEn: Required by a law or rule.
words.exampleDailyEn: Wearing a helmet is mandatory at this climbing centre.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Mandatory safety training can reduce workplace accidents by ensuring that all employees understand potential risks.

words.definitionEn: to make an agreement or decision legally invalid
words.exampleDailyEn: This missing signature could nullify the entire rental agreement.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Rising energy consumption could nullify the environmental benefits achieved through improvements in industrial efficiency.

words.definitionEn: A formal promise to tell the truth or fulfil a duty.
words.exampleDailyEn: The witness took an oath before answering any questions.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public officials who swear an oath to serve society should remain accountable for their decisions and conduct.

words.definitionEn: To require someone to do something legally or morally.
words.exampleDailyEn: Does this agreement obligate me to pay every month?
words.exampleIeltsEn: Environmental regulations obligate manufacturers to dispose of hazardous waste safely rather than transfer responsibility to local communities.

words.definitionEn: To force someone out of a position or place.
words.exampleDailyEn: Club members voted to oust their unpopular chair.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Shareholders may seek to oust company directors who repeatedly fail to meet environmental commitments or financial targets.

words.definitionEn: to make an activity illegal
words.exampleDailyEn: The new rules outlaw dumping rubbish beside the river.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should outlaw the sale of products made from endangered species to discourage illegal hunting.

words.definitionEn: To use authority to reject or reverse a decision or objection.
words.exampleDailyEn: The manager overruled my request to close the shop early.
words.exampleIeltsEn: National authorities may overrule local planning decisions when major infrastructure projects serve the wider public interest.

words.definitionEn: to remove a ruler or government from power
words.exampleDailyEn: The film follows citizens who overthrow an unfair ruler.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Economic hardship can weaken public support for a government and encourage attempts to overthrow it.

words.definitionEn: Allowed by a rule, law, or accepted standard
words.exampleDailyEn: Is it permissible to take photographs inside this museum?
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should establish clear limits on permissible emissions to protect public health in industrial areas.

words.definitionEn: A serious promise to do or provide something
words.exampleDailyEn: We made a pledge to keep the beach clean.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities have pledged to improve public transport and reduce traffic congestion over the next decade.

words.definitionEn: Give up control, possession or a right to something.
words.exampleDailyEn: She reluctantly relinquished her seat beside the window.
words.exampleIeltsEn: National governments may be reluctant to relinquish control over energy policy to international organisations.

words.definitionEn: To protect someone or something from harm or loss.
words.exampleDailyEn: These padded covers safeguard the furniture during the move.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should introduce stronger regulations to safeguard personal information collected by online services and mobile applications.

words.definitionEn: Careful examination of something, especially to find faults or problems.
words.exampleDailyEn: The jeweller examined the ring with intense scrutiny.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public spending should be subject to independent scrutiny to ensure that resources are used efficiently and fairly.

words.definitionEn: To state a requirement clearly as part of an agreement
words.exampleDailyEn: The rental rules stipulate that pets must stay downstairs.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Employment contracts should stipulate working hours clearly to prevent disputes between employers and their staff.

words.definitionEn: highest in rank, authority, or importance
words.exampleDailyEn: The council has supreme authority over the island.
words.exampleIeltsEn: In many countries, the supreme court can review whether new legislation complies with the constitution.

words.definitionEn: cruel government that uses power without limits
words.exampleDailyEn: The film follows a village struggling against a ruler's tyranny.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Independent courts and a free press can help prevent tyranny by holding political leaders accountable.

words.definitionEn: To support and maintain a principle, right, or standard
words.exampleDailyEn: Our coach always tries to uphold fair play.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Independent courts help uphold citizens' rights by ensuring that public authorities act within the law.

words.definitionEn: An official court decision about whether someone is guilty.
words.exampleDailyEn: What is your verdict on my homemade soup?
words.exampleIeltsEn: A jury should reach its verdict solely on the evidence presented during the trial.

words.definitionEn: Official power to reject a decision, or its use.
words.exampleDailyEn: The club president used her veto to stop the purchase.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Giving every member a veto can protect minority interests but may also delay urgent collective decisions.

words.definitionEn: A process of voting, usually in secret.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our club chose its new chair by secret ballot.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A secret ballot allows citizens to express their political preferences without fear of pressure from others.

words.definitionEn: an administrative system run by officials following established rules
words.exampleDailyEn: My aunt works within the city's large bureaucracy.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Reducing unnecessary bureaucracy could help small businesses obtain permits more quickly without weakening essential safety standards.

words.definitionEn: an official count of people that collects information about them
words.exampleDailyEn: We completed the census form at our kitchen table.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Census data help governments plan housing, schools and healthcare services according to changing population needs.

words.definitionEn: A room used for a particular, often official, purpose.
words.exampleDailyEn: We waited outside the chamber while the council met.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The upper chamber of parliament reviews proposed laws before they can receive final approval.

words.definitionEn: relating to a town or city and its administration
words.exampleDailyEn: The mayor welcomed visitors outside the new civic centre.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools can strengthen civic responsibility by encouraging students to participate in projects that benefit their local communities.

words.definitionEn: a senior army or air force officer
words.exampleDailyEn: The colonel greeted the soldiers outside the camp.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A colonel coordinated the military's emergency response, ensuring that isolated communities received food and medical supplies.

words.definitionEn: opposing social progress and wanting older political arrangements restored
words.exampleDailyEn: My uncle called the proposal reactionary and unfair.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Critics argue that reactionary policies can reverse social progress by restoring outdated restrictions on individual freedom.

words.definitionEn: To officially end a law, agreement, or established right.
words.exampleDailyEn: The council voted to abrogate the outdated parking regulation.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should not abrogate international agreements without carefully considering the consequences for regional stability and public trust.

words.definitionEn: to formally agree to a request, demand, or proposal
words.exampleDailyEn: The landlord finally acceded to our request for repairs.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments may accede to public demands for greater transparency when trust in national institutions declines.

words.definitionEn: To make an official decision about a dispute
words.exampleDailyEn: An independent expert will adjudicate our dispute over the repairs.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Independent bodies should adjudicate disputes between consumers and businesses to ensure that complaints receive fair and consistent treatment.

words.definitionEn: to stop resisting and accept another person's demands
words.exampleDailyEn: After hours of arguing, we capitulated and ordered pizza.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should not capitulate to commercial pressure when public health and environmental protection are at stake.

words.definitionEn: to officially cancel an earlier order
words.exampleDailyEn: The manager countermanded the order to close the shop.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local officials may countermand evacuation orders only when reliable evidence shows that the danger has passed.

words.definitionEn: Impossible to change, cancel, or take back.
words.exampleDailyEn: Once you sign, your decision becomes legally irrevocable.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should consult local communities before making irrevocable decisions about the destruction of historic buildings.

words.definitionEn: Peaceful in nature or intended to avoid conflict
words.exampleDailyEn: Her pacific manner helped calm the argument at dinner.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A pacific approach to international disputes prioritises negotiation and cooperation rather than threats or military action.

words.definitionEn: a special right belonging to a particular person or group
words.exampleDailyEn: Choosing the final design is the team leader's prerogative.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Decisions about public spending should not be the exclusive prerogative of a small group of officials.

words.definitionEn: Officially cancel a decision, agreement, or rule.
words.exampleDailyEn: The club rescinded its decision to close the pool.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The council agreed to rescind the parking restrictions after residents raised concerns about access to local shops.

words.definitionEn: to break a law, rule, or moral boundary
words.exampleDailyEn: Players who transgress the rules may leave the game.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Companies that transgress environmental laws should face penalties proportionate to the damage they cause.

words.definitionEn: Using power cruelly and unfairly to control others.
words.exampleDailyEn: The club members finally challenged their tyrannical leader.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Independent courts can help prevent tyrannical rule by limiting government power and protecting basic rights.
